title: file/input handling: multipart support, tool/file payload limits, content-type validation, OpenAI-compat updates
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Add robust file/input handling across the Redwood API surface to support multipart uploads for file attachments, enforce tool/file payload limits to protect the serving fleet, and strengthen content-type validation for OpenAI-compat requests. This change addresses recurring incidents where large binary payloads and incorrect Content-Type headers caused streaming stalls and excessive KV/cache memory pressure. It also aligns the OpenAI compatibility layer with upstream expectations for multipart/form-data semantics and file size errors.

What this PR does (summary):
- Add multipart/form-data parsing support for /v1/files and /v1/chat/completions endpoints in the OpenAI compatibility layer.
- Introduce configurable per-route file/tool payload limits (default 50MB for files, 5MB for tool payloads) with clear error codes and Retry-After when appropriate.
- Content-Type and charset validation for text inputs, JSON bodies, and file attachments with explicit error responses for malformed headers.
- Streaming stability improvements: reject oversized attachments early, avoid buffering full payloads into memory, and wire size checks into request body streaming path.
- Update client-facing error messages to use OpenAI-compatible error structures where applicable.
- Add tests (unit + integration) and e2e for multipart uploads, limit enforcement, and content-type corner cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Multipart parser implemented and integrated into OpenAI-compat middleware
- [x] Size limit configuration and enforcement added to api-gateway and runtime request pipeline
- [x] Error mapping to OpenAI-compatible error payloads
- [x] Unit, integration, and e2e tests added
- [x] Docs and examples updated in redwood-docs quickstart
- [x] Rollout plan included (gradual config enablement + telemetry)

Testing and rollout: Unit tests and integration tests were added under redwood-openai-compat and runtime. An internal canary job was run for 48h with multipart enabled on a small fraction of traffic and telemetry showed a 98% success rate; oversized payloads were rejected with 413 quickly. Rollout will be controlled via a feature flag enabling multipart parsing and limits per-tenant, with fallback to legacy behavior if necessary.

Backward compatibility: Default limits are conservative and configurable; existing clients continue to work unless they exceed size limits. Error responses were chosen to maintain OpenAI compatibility for SDKs that expect structured errors.

Related: linear ENG-1024 (multipart & limits), ENG-1032 (streaming stability).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we make limits configurable per-tenant and per-route? Also, prefer returning OpenAI-style 413 error with type 'invalid_request_error' so SDKs surface consistently.

Aisha Khan (author): Addressed — limits are per-tenant and per-route; default values live in helm values and can be overridden via tenant config. Error mapping updated to 'invalid_request_error' for 413 responses.
Priya Patel: Concern about streaming to disk on high QPS — do we have IO backpressure controls to avoid saturating disks?

Aisha Khan: Added an in-memory threshold (configurable) above which we spill to tempstore; runtime enforces max concurrent spills and exposes metrics for disk spill saturation. Documentation added to observability pack.
Diego Morales: suggest adding a quick benchmark for 1MB/5MB/50MB uploads to show latency impact when streaming vs buffering.
Aisha Khan: Added micro-benchmarks in perf-canary and included summary in PR description; no meaningful latency regression under normal QPS, spikes are handled via early reject.

release_notes: Add multipart file upload support and per-route payload limits. Configurable defaults: file_max_size=50MB, tool_payload_max_size=5MB. Improvements to streaming stability and OpenAI-compatible error responses for oversized or malformed inputs.
discussion: PM note (from roadmap sync): This PR reduces incident surface for large attachment uploads and allows us to support file-based evals more safely.
SRE note: Added alerts for high rate of 413/invalid_request_error and disk_spill_saturation to prevent noisy failures during rollout.
Docs: Quickstart example added. API consumers should be aware of default limits and can request higher quotas via support.
